Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that becoming a new mother can be a life-changing and sometimes overwhelming experience. It's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there's anything we can do to support you better. The purpose of this assessment is to check in with you about your emotional well-being during the postpartum period, and it's completely confidential. Everything we discuss today will remain between us, and I want to assure you that this is a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself freely.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of your feelings and experiences over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. This will give us a chance to connect and understand what's been going on for you since having your baby.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that there's no right or wrong answer to any of these questions. I'm here to listen, support, and provide guidance, not to judge. If at any point you feel uncomfortable or need to take a break, please don't hesitate to let me know.

Let's get started with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do?

(sighing) Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, but it's just been so hard to adjust to all of this. I used to enjoy doing things like reading, taking walks, and spending time with friends, but lately, I just don't seem to have the energy or interest in doing those things like I used to. Even simple things like taking a shower or getting dressed feel like a chore. (pausing, looking down) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, you know? I'm not really enjoying it like I thought I would. And that makes me feel guilty, like I'm not doing something right. (looking up, tears welling up in my eyes) Sometimes I feel like I'm just not good enough, like I'm failing my baby. (voice cracking) It's hard to explain, but I just feel really sad and discouraged a lot of the time.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking my head) Not as much as I used to, to be honest. I mean, I'll have moments where I'll laugh at something my baby does, or my husband will make a joke and I'll smile, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor a bit. Even when I do laugh, it doesn't feel as deep or as fulfilling as it used to. And sometimes, even when things are funny, I'll just feel anxious or worried instead of being able to laugh and enjoy the moment. (sighing) It's like my mind is always on my baby's safety and well-being, and it's hard for me to relax and just enjoy the funny side of things. (pausing, looking down) I miss feeling carefree and able to laugh without worrying about everything.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head slightly) Not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, everything just feels like a chore. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting a friend for coffee, just feel like too much effort now. (sighing) I've been having trouble sleeping, and when I do sleep, I wake up feeling anxious and worried about the day ahead. It's hard for me to think about things I'm supposed to be looking forward to, like my baby's milestones or special events, because I just feel so overwhelmed all the time. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I'll think about something that's coming up, like a doctor's appointment or a visit from my family, and instead of feeling excited or happy, I just feel anxious and worried about how I'm going to get everything done. (voice barely above a whisper) It's like I've lost my sense of excitement and anticipation, and everything just feels like a burden.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If my baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm feeling tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. (sighing) I just feel like I'm constantly questioning myself and my abilities as a mother. I'll think about all the things I could be doing differently, and I'll beat myself up over them. (pausing, looking up) Even when my husband or family members try to reassure me that I'm doing a good job, I just can't seem to shake the feeling that I'm not good enough. (voice filled with self-doubt) I feel like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and then I'll be able to say, "See, I knew I wasn't cut out for this." (shaking my head) It's a really hard feeling to explain, but it's just this constant sense of self-doubt and blame that I'm carrying around with me all the time.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yes. This is me all the time. I worry about everything. I worry that my baby is going to get sick, or that I'm not feeding her enough, or that I'm not changing her diaper often enough. I worry that I'm not doing enough to stimulate her development, or that I'm not giving her enough attention. (taking a deep breath) And it's not just about my baby. I worry about my relationship with my husband, and whether we're going to be able to handle the stress of having a new baby. I worry about how I'm going to balance being a mom with being a person, and whether I'm going to lose myself in all of this. (looking up, eyes wide with anxiety) Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just be hit with this wave of fear and worry. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to panic. (shaking my head) It's like my brain is just constantly looking for things to worry about, and it's exhausting. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I just wish I could turn it off, you know? Just be able to relax and enjoy this time with my baby, without all the anxiety and worry.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just me, alone with my baby, and yet I'll feel like I'm in danger somehow. (shaking my head) It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I'll be awake at night, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear. I'll be thinking, "What if something happens to my baby? What if I'm not doing enough to keep her safe?" (voice trembling) And then I'll start to feel like I'm going to lose control, like I'm going to panic and not be able to take care of my baby. (taking a deep breath) It's a really terrifying feeling, and it's hard to shake once it starts. (looking down, tears welling up in my eyes) I just feel so overwhelmed and scared, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Oh, yes. That's exactly how I've been feeling. Like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. (sighing) Taking care of my baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly worrying about her, and trying to make sure she's okay, and it's just overwhelming. (looking down, feeling tears well up in my eyes) And on top of that, I'm trying to manage my own emotions, and my relationships with my husband and family, and it just feels like too much. (shaking my head) I feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Some days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to feel like I'm going to break down. Like I just can't do it anymore. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) And that's a really scary feeling, because I know I need to be strong for my baby. I need to be able to take care of her, and provide for her, and be there for her. But some days, it just feels like too much.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes, that's me. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping lately. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about all the things I need to do, and worrying about my baby, and just feeling really overwhelmed. (sighing) Even when I do fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious and worried. It's like my brain just won't turn off, and I'm constantly thinking about all the things that could go wrong. (looking down, feeling tears well up in my eyes) And it's not just the sleep itself, it's the feeling of being unhappy and unfulfilled that's keeping me awake. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really enjoying it. I'm not really feeling like myself, and that's a really hard thing to deal with. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll wake up in the morning, feeling exhausted, and just think to myself, "How am I going to get through this day?" (shaking my head) It's a really hard feeling to explain, but it's just this constant sense of unhappiness and overwhelm that's affecting every aspect of my life, including my sleep. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish I could find a way to break this cycle, and start feeling like myself again.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes, that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I have this beautiful baby, and I love her so much, but sometimes it just feels like everything is too much for me. (pausing, looking down) I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, and all the things I'm worried about, and it just feels like too much. (tears welling up in my eyes) I'll start to cry, and I won't be able to stop. It's like my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and anything can set me off. (sighing) Even happy things, like when my baby smiles at me, can make me feel sad. I'll think, "Oh, she's smiling at me, but what if I'm not doing enough to make her happy?" or "What if I'm not a good enough mom?" (shaking my head) It's just this constant cycle of negative thoughts and feelings, and it's hard to break free from it. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish I could find a way to be happy again, to enjoy this time with my baby without all the sadness and worry.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling tears well up in my eyes) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like I'm just so overwhelmed and sad all the time, and I don't know how to deal with it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start to feel this wave of emotions wash over me. I'll think about how hard it is to be a mom, and how I'm not doing enough, and how I'm just not good enough. (tears streaming down my face) And then I'll just start to cry. It's like my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and anything can set me off. (sobbing) I've been crying in the shower, I've been crying while I'm feeding my baby, I've even been crying while I'm driving. It's just like I'm constantly on the verge of tears, and I don't know how to stop it. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish I could find a way to be happy again, to enjoy this time with my baby without all the sadness and worry. (sobbing) I feel like I'm just so alone in this, like I'm the only one who's feeling this way. (looking down, feeling ashamed) And that makes me feel even more guilty, like I'm not a good enough mom because I'm not happy all the time.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, looking down, feeling a sense of shame and vulnerability) Yes... (whispering) I've had those thoughts. They're fleeting, but they're there. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to make it stop, my mind will just start to wander to really dark places. (looking up, feeling a sense of fear) I'll think about how I just want to escape, how I just want to make all the pain and sadness go away. (pausing, feeling tears well up in my eyes) And sometimes, those thoughts will turn to... (pausing, struggling to say the words) ...to harming myself. (looking down, feeling a sense of shame) I know it's not rational, I know it's not something I would ever actually do, but the thought is there, and it's scary. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I feel like I'm losing control, like I'm just barely holding on. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish I could find a way to make those thoughts go away, to find some peace and happiness again. (sobbing) I don't want to feel like this anymore, I don't want to be a burden to my loved ones. I just want to be a good mom, and a happy person, but it feels like that's so far out of reach right now.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities, difficulty coping with responsibilities and emotions, anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, sleep difficulties linked to mood and anxiety, feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and self-doubt, and crying spells and emotional reactivity. The patient also reports having thoughts of self-harm, which is a significant concern requiring immediate attention and follow-up.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 28, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates a noticeable decrease in their ability to laugh and see the funny side of things, with moments of laughter feeling less deep and fulfilling, and anxiety often overriding humor.</sym>, <sym>the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong tendency to blame themselves unnecessarily, constantly questioning their abilities as a mother and experiencing self-doubt, which aligns with the option 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense feelings of panic and fear, even when there is no apparent threat, indicating a high level of distress.</sym>, <sym>The patient expresses feeling overwhelmed, exhausted, and like they're 'drowning in responsibilities', indicating a strong sense of being unable to cope with their situation, matching the 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been feeling sad and miserable a lot lately, and that these feelings are persistent and overwhelming, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of self-harm, describing them as fleeting but present when feeling overwhelmed and sad, which aligns with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses suggest a high level of emotional distress, anxiety, and difficulty coping with postpartum responsibilities, consistent with the <med>Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)</med> guidelines and <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The presence of persistent <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, and <sym>thoughts of self-harm</sym> indicates a need for further evaluation and support. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices to help manage <sym>sleep difficulties</sym>
3. Support patient in developing coping strategies for <sym>anxiety</sym> and <sym>panic</sym>
4. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum depression</med> support and education
5. Monitor patient's <sym>thoughts of self-harm</sym> and adjust treatment plan as needed
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
